title: Evaluation and cocycle for an internal-Hom target changed with coefficients
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of characteristic $p$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and the finite rings $A_j=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^j$ for $j\ge1$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $X$ be a separated finite-type $k$-scheme [def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-proper-morphism]. Use the ordinary module-sheaf derived categories on the small etale or pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules]. Bounded constructibility means [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes] on the etale site and [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility] on the pro-etale site. A complex has Tor interval $[a,b]$ if its derived tensor with every degree-zero module sheaf has zero cohomology outside $[a,b]$; $D^b_{ctf}$ means bounded constructible with some finite Tor interval [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. For $i\ge j\ge1$, write $S_{i,j}=-\otimes^L_{A_i}A_j$ for the quotient scalar extension [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings].

Fix one of the two sites. Write $H_j(U,V)=R\mathcal Hom_{A_j}(U,V)$ [def-pur-derived-internal-hom], with its tensor-Hom evaluation. Fix $N\ge1$, objects $\Omega_j\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A_j)$ for $1\le j\le N$, and isomorphisms $u_{i,j}:S_{i,j}\Omega_i\xrightarrow{\sim}\Omega_j$ for $N\ge i\ge j\ge1$. Assume $u_{i,i}=1$ and $u_{i,r}=u_{j,r}\circ S_{j,r}(u_{i,j})$, using the canonical scalar units and reassociations [lem-fix-operation-reduction]. Let $v^{i,j}_{U,V}$ be the evaluation-defined internal-Hom comparison of [thm-coef-finite-hom]. For $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A_i)$ define
$$h^{i,j}_{K,\Omega}=H_j(S_{i,j}K,u_{i,j})\circ v^{i,j}_{K,\Omega_i}:S_{i,j}H_i(K,\Omega_i)\longrightarrow H_j(S_{i,j}K,\Omega_j).$$
These are natural isomorphisms, contravariant in $K$, with the following specified evaluation identity:
$$\operatorname{ev}_{S_{i,j}K,\Omega_j}\circ(h^{i,j}_{K,\Omega}\otimes1)=u_{i,j}\circ S_{i,j}(\operatorname{ev}_{K,\Omega_i}),$$
where $S_{i,j}(H_i(K,\Omega_i)\otimes^L_{A_i}K)$ is identified with $S_{i,j}H_i(K,\Omega_i)\otimes^L_{A_j}S_{i,j}K$. For $i\ge j\ge r$ they satisfy
$$h^{i,r}_{K,\Omega}=h^{j,r}_{S_{i,j}K,\Omega}\circ S_{j,r}(h^{i,j}_{K,\Omega}),\qquad h^{i,i}_{K,\Omega}=1.$$
The construction is natural also in a morphism of target families $(\Omega_j,u_{i,j})$. The targets are arbitrary finite-Tor constructible complexes; no assertion that they are geometric dualizing objects is assumed.

proof.text: On the etale site, [lem-coef-finite-hom-domain-calculus] gives $S_{i,j}K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A_j)$; on the pro-etale site this is the first assertion of [lem-coef-closed-scalar-domains], applied with $L=E$ and the quotient map. Thus all subsequent applications are in the required domains. Apply [thm-coef-finite-hom] to $(K,\Omega_i)$: $v^{i,j}_{K,\Omega_i}$ is an isomorphism, with the specified evaluation, naturality and successive-quotient equations. Write $K_j=S_{i,j}K$ and suppress only the canonical scalar reassociations throughout.

source.place: 'Apply thm-coef-finite-hom with second argument'; domains and specified comparison

proof.text: By the bifunctoriality in [def-pur-derived-internal-hom], $H_j(K_j,u_{i,j})$ has inverse $H_j(K_j,u_{i,j}^{-1})$. Consequently $h^{i,j}_{K,\Omega}$ is invertible. For $f:K\to L$, naturality of $v$ in [thm-coef-finite-hom] and commutation of the two variables of $H$ give $H_j(S_{i,j}f,1)\circ h^{i,j}_{L,\Omega}=h^{i,j}_{K,\Omega}\circ S_{i,j}H_i(f,1)$. Indeed first commute $H_j(Sf,1)$ past $H_j(SL,u_{i,j})$, and then use the naturality square for $v_{-,\Omega_i}$. This is contravariant naturality.

source.place: 'The resulting map is d'; invertibility and contravariant naturality

proof.text: Evaluation is the counit of the tensor-Hom adjunction used in [thm-coef-finite-hom], hence is natural in its target. With $u=u_{i,j}$, this is $\mathrm{ev}_{K_j,\Omega_j}\circ(H_j(K_j,u)\otimes1)=u\circ\mathrm{ev}_{K_j,S_{i,j}\Omega_i}$. Compose this equality with $v^{i,j}_{K,\Omega_i}\otimes1$. The evaluation equation of the same theorem replaces the last evaluation composed with $v\otimes1$ by $S_{i,j}(\mathrm{ev}_{K,\Omega_i})$, under its specified tensor comparison. This gives exactly the claimed evaluation identity.

source.place: 'Evaluation compatibility follows from the two comparisons already proved'

proof.text:
Fix $i\ge j\ge r$. Set $F=S_{i,j}$, $G=S_{j,r}$, $Q=FK$, and write $v^F,v^G$ for the specified comparisons. Naturality in the second variable in [thm-coef-finite-hom], applied to $u_{i,j}:F\Omega_i\to\Omega_j$, says $v^G_{Q,\Omega_j}\circ G(H_j(Q,u_{i,j}))=H_r(GQ,G u_{i,j})\circ v^G_{Q,F\Omega_i}$. Expanding the proposed composite therefore gives
$$\begin{aligned}h^{j,r}_{Q,\Omega}\circ G(h^{i,j}_{K,\Omega})&=H_r(GQ,u_{j,r})\circ H_r(GQ,G u_{i,j})\circ v^G_{Q,F\Omega_i}\circ G(v^F_{K,\Omega_i})\\&=H_r(GQ,u_{j,r}\circ G u_{i,j})\circ v^{i,r}_{K,\Omega_i}\\&=H_r(S_{i,r}K,u_{i,r})\circ v^{i,r}_{K,\Omega_i}=h^{i,r}_{K,\Omega}.\end{aligned}$$
The second equality is Hom functoriality [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] and the quotient cocycle for $v$ in the cited theorem; the third is precisely the assumed target-family cocycle. All equations use the same scalar associators as that theorem, so the two occurrences of $GQ$ are identified with $S_{i,r}K$ by the specified identification.

source.place: 'The cocycle is their quotient cocycle'; explicit target-map calculation

proof.text:
For $i=j$, scalar extension and its tensor comparison are identified with the identity by the canonical scalar unit. The identity on $H_i(K,\Omega_i)$ has transpose $\mathrm{ev}_{K,\Omega_i}$, so uniqueness of the evaluation transpose in [thm-coef-finite-hom] gives $v^{i,i}_{K,\Omega_i}=1$. Since $u_{i,i}=1$, functoriality gives $h^{i,i}=1$. Finally let $t_j:\Omega_j\to\Omega'_j$ be a morphism of target families, meaning $t_j\circ u_{i,j}=u'_{i,j}\circ S_{i,j}t_i$. Covariant naturality of $v$ and Hom functoriality give
$$\begin{aligned}H_j(K_j,t_j)\circ h^{i,j}_{K,\Omega}&=H_j(K_j,t_j\circ u_{i,j})\circ v_{K,\Omega_i}^{i,j}\\&=H_j(K_j,u'_{i,j})\circ H_j(K_j,S_{i,j}t_i)\circ v_{K,\Omega_i}^{i,j}\\&=h^{i,j}_{K,\Omega'}\circ S_{i,j}H_i(K,t_i).\end{aligned}$$
This proves naturality for arbitrary target-family morphisms, without requiring the $t_j$ to be invertible or the targets to be dualizing objects.
